text: FOR ALL: Progress report. (So..... how would you say things are going?) Sen. Wintrow, from the outside, it seems like things are getting testy in the joint budget committee. Is that a fair assessment? Sen. Lent, as a chairman, what’s your perspective on how the joint committee is approaching this year’s budgets? Director Wolff, we heard again today at least one senator in the health and welfare budget debate confused over why the state isn’t tapping into rainy day funds to address some of this. Utilizing rainy day funds wasn’t part of the governor’s proposal at the start of the session. Is he open to it now? Rep. Monks: We’ve heard disagreements even among the nine House Republicans who sit on the House Appropriations Committee. Where is the caucus as a whole on the budget proposals? FOR EVERYONE: How about the budget setting process? Are your caucuses generally satisfied? Director Wolff, how are communications between the Division of Financial Management and lawmakers? IN OTHER NEWS.... Rep. Monks, after debate on Wednesday, you made a motion to suspend the rule that would allow the minority party to submit a report for the record. Why? What were the factors? (If he brings up the length of the report) Is it outlined in the rule how long a minority report has to be? (Open up for discussion, or ask Sen. Wintrow for her reaction) Sen. Lent, so much of the conversation has focused on the budget this year. How are things going on the policy side? (If he doesn’t bring it up) You’ve held town halls around the state about public education. What are you hearing from Idahoans about education, and what they hope it looks like in the future? Are there any specific policy proposals you have in mind? FOR ALL: What do you hope the legislature addresses before you adjourn for the session?
